evidence: src/application/inventory-service.ts: InventoryService depends only on ProductRepository and returns ProductSnapshot through product.toSnapshot(). This is the same pattern OrderService uses with OrderSnapshot.
src/application/order-service.ts: placeOrder relies on the domain for its stock and quantity rules (product.canReserve, product.reserve, assertPositiveInteger) and does not re-implement them.
src/application/order-service.ts: changeState returns this.cancel(id) when the target is 'cancelled', so the release-stock logic exists only in cancel().

Minor duplication: the product lookup-and-throw NotFoundError guard appears in InventoryService.getStock, inline in OrderService.placeOrder, and in the private OrderService.requireProduct. placeOrder does not use requireProduct.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module covers one concern: application use cases for the order and inventory domain. Both services depend on the same domain ports and return snapshots in the same way, so neither one goes around the repository or snapshot abstractions. The domain rules stay in the domain objects: stock is checked through Product.canReserve, reserve, ship and release, state changes go through Order.transitionTo and nextState, and quantities are validated with assertPositiveInteger. The services coordinate these calls and do not re-implement them. OrderService.changeState passes cancellation to cancel(), so the stock-release logic is written only once.

There is one minor problem. The guard that looks up a product and throws NotFoundError("Product ... not found") is written three times: in InventoryService.getStock, inline inside OrderService.placeOrder, and in OrderService.requireProduct. placeOrder does not use the requireProduct helper defined in its own class. This is a small, low-risk lookup guard, not a business rule or invariant, so I'm treating it as a cleanup item rather than a failure. That is why my confidence is moderate.
